title: Rename prefork-rs to clid framework
description:
Rename project from prefork-rs to clid — a framework for building CLI→daemon execution hand-off systems.

## Architecture
- **clid** — umbrella crate, re-exports everything
- **clid-context** — serializable execution context (rkyv)
- **clid-discovery** — socket discovery with feature-gated strategies (local, xdg, env)
- **clid-client** — thin client: serialize context, pass FDs, exit
- **clid-daemon** — receive, deserialize, dispatch to async handlers. Optional prefork feature
- **examples/clidd** — reference daemon (was pfd)
- **examples/clidc** — reference client (was pfc)

## Tasks
- [ ] Rename workspace from prefork-rs to clid
- [ ] Rename context → clid-context
- [ ] Rename discovery → clid-discovery, add feature flags
- [ ] Extract pfc internals → clid-client library
- [ ] Extract pfd internals → clid-daemon library, optional prefork feature
- [ ] Create examples/clidd and examples/clidc
- [ ] Create clid umbrella crate
- [ ] Rewrite README
- [ ] Update all Cargo.toml inter-crate deps
- [ ] Verify build + tests pass
notes: Completed rename. Old pfc/pfd/context/discovery crates replaced with clid-{context,discovery,client,daemon} library crates, clid umbrella crate, and examples/clidd+clidc reference binaries. Feature-gated discovery strategies. Optional prefork feature on clid-daemon. All 20 tests pass, clean build.

title: INTEGRATION: Wire deserialize, dispatch, and commands into main loop
description:
Connect CONTEXT-DESERIALIZE, CMD-DISPATCH, and command execution into the daemon's main receive loop.

**Components:**
- Initialize CmdRegistry with registered commands
- On receive: deserialize bytes → dispatch to command function → execute
- Handle errors at each stage gracefully
- Log command execution

**Main Flow:**
1. Receive bytes + FDs from UnixDatagram
2. Deserialize to EXECUTION-CONTEXT (CONTEXT-DESERIALIZE)
3. Extract command name from EXECUTION-CONTEXT.command
4. Dispatch via CMD-DISPATCH to registered function
5. Command function executes with EXECUTION-CONTEXT + FDs
6. Log result or error

**Behavior:**
- Each connection goes through full pipeline
- Errors logged but don't crash daemon
- Unknown commands handled gracefully
- FDs properly managed through execution

**Short-names:**
- INTEGRATION: Full receive-to-execute pipeline

**Dependencies:**
- pfd-daemon-context-deserialize
- pfd-daemon-cmd-dispatch
- pfd-daemon-cmd-add

**Acceptance:**
- Full pipeline works end-to-end
- pfc client can execute "add" command successfully
- Errors handled at each stage

- Fire-and-forget model (no connection needed)

- context library for ExecutionContext

1. Build ExecutionContext with cwd, command, args

3. Create FD array [stdin, stdout, stderr]
4. Send bytes + FDs via UnixDatagram::send_with_fd
5. Exit - daemon handles execution

title: SD-NOTIFY: Systemd service notification support
description:
Add sd-notify support for notifying systemd when daemon is ready.

**Implementation:**
- Use libsystemd or sd-notify crate
- Send READY=1 on successful startup
- Send STATUS= for state changes
- Support WATCHDOG=1 for watchdog pings
- Support main PID tracking

**Components:**
- sd-notify integration
- Startup notification sequence
- Watchdog ping handling
- Graceful shutdown handling

**Use Case:**
When pfd starts as a systemd service, systemd waits for READY notification before considering service started. Without this, service starts in race condition.

**Flow:**
1. Bind socket
2. Start listener
3. Send 'READY=1' via sd_notify
4. Systemd marks service as started
5. Enter main loop

**Extra Features:**
- Support 'RELOADING=1' before hot reload
- 'STOPPING=1' before shutdown
- 'STATUS=...' for detailed status updates
notes:
Preserve service READY/STATUS/WATCHDOG notification scope as independent notification tools; fdstore child covers custody-specific behavior.

title: Blocking proxy and result
description:
Forward argv including help; server parses; transferred stdin/out/err work through pipes/redirection; client exits with result; define signal/disconnect scope without claiming full shell job-control transparency.

Architecture: design/fd-handoff/architecture0.gpt6a.md E5.2
design:
Add support for returning values from child processes back to the parent. This will require:
- A mechanism to serialize return values (likely using serde or similar)
- A way to send the return value through IPC (inter-process communication)
- Parent must wait for the result before continuing

Important tradeoff: The client will be forced to wait for the result, which blocks execution until the child completes. This is a synchronous operation.
acceptance_criteria: Forward argv including help; server parses; transferred stdin/out/err work through pipes/redirection; client exits with result; define signal/disconnect scope without claiming full shell job-control transparency.

title: SOCKET-DGRAM: Switch from UnixStream to UnixDatagram
description:
Switch daemon from SOCK_STREAM to SOCK_DGRAM Unix domain socket.

**Implementation:**
- Replace UnixListener/UnixStream with UnixDatagram
- Use fire-and-forget message model (no connection)
- Simplifies client - no connect() needed
- Send file descriptors with discrete messages
- Use spawn_blocking for recv_with_fd on DGRAM socket

**Components:**
- tokio::net::UnixDatagram for message-based sockets
- sendfd::RecvWithFd for FD reception
- Unsafe conversion from raw FD to std UnixDatagram

**Benefits:**
- No connection state management
- Preserves message boundaries
- Simpler client lifecycle (short-lived processes)
- File descriptors travel with discrete messages

**Trade-offs:**
- No ordering guarantees
- Messages can be dropped (need retry in client)
- Requires spawn_blocking for recv_with_fd
close_reason: Switched from UnixStream to UnixDatagram for fire-and-forget client model

- Returns first socket that accepts connection

title: FD-TRANSFER: Crate for file descriptor transfer
description:
Crate library for file descriptor transfer over Unix domain sockets.

This library provides safe, ergonomic file descriptor passing using ancillary data:

**Capabilities:**
- Send/receive multiple file descriptors atomically
- Unix domain socket wrapper with ancillary data support
- Descriptor lifecycle and ownership management
- Error handling for partial/failed transfers
- Zero-copy descriptor passing where possible

**API Goals:**
- Simple `send_fds(&socket, &[FileDescriptor])` interface
- `recv_fds(&socket) -> Result<Vec<FileDescriptor>>`
- Atomic transfer guarantees for multiple descriptors
- Clear error types for debugging transfer failures

**Use Cases:**
- Passing stdin/stdout/stderr between processes
- Transferring arbitrary file handles (files, sockets, pipes)
- Pre-fork daemon patterns where child needs parent's resources

Based on `sendfd` crate research but with higher-level API and better ergonomics.

- XDG-project mode: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pfd.<project-name>.sock`

title: PFC-CLIENT: Minimal client for execution transfer
description:
PreFork Client (PFC) - minimal lightweight client that transfers execution context to daemon.

Philosophy: Keep client incredibly small and simple. Find daemon quickly, transfer context, terminate.

Responsibilities:
- Socket discovery with multiple strategies
- Auto-launch daemon if not found (--create flag)
- Serialize execution context
- Transfer context and file descriptors via socket
- Minimal error handling and feedback

- Parse and validate execution context

title: EXECUTION-CONTEXT: Execution context serialization subsystem
description:
Execution context serialization and validation.

**Components:**
- Serialization format for socket transfer (bincode)
- Working directory validation and change
- Argument array encoding and validation
- Security validation before execution
- Descriptor mapping and restoration

**Flow:**
1. Client serializes execution context
2. Transfer over Unix socket with ancillary data
3. Daemon receives and validates context
4. Change to working directory
5. Spawn child process with transferred descriptors
6. Execute command with provided arguments
close_reason: Created context library with ExecutionContext struct using rkyv for zero-copy serialization

title: DAEMON-LIFECYCLE: Daemon lifecycle management subsystem
description:
Daemon process lifecycle management for background operations.

**Components:**
- Double-fork daemonization for true background process
- PID file creation and locking in XDG locations
- Process group management
- Signal handling for graceful shutdown
- Daemon health checking via PID files
- Auto-launch daemon functionality (--create/-C flag)

**Lifecycle:**
1. Spawn via double-fork
2. Create PID file in XDG location with lock
3. Start Unix domain socket listener
4. Accept execution contexts from clients
5. Handle signals (SIGTERM, SIGINT) for clean shutdown
6. Cleanup PID file on exit

**Guarantees:**
- Single instance enforcement via PID lock
- Clean termination of active executions
- Proper cleanup of resources on exit
